soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 2 and Theorem 3
soundness_flags.one_line: Their universal quantifiers range over arbitrary input tables while demanding witnesses in fixed \(\mathfrak M_\epsilon\) and \(\mathfrak R^\circ_{\epsilon,\eta}\); restrict to compatible inputs induced by \(\mathfrak M_\epsilon\) and quantify \(\eta>0\) existentially (or state it as a fixed uniform interior regime).

accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The integration theorem is considered only as: EXT-ID is complete on compatible inputs conditional on affirmative resolutions of those three named premises; the field-level focal object remains the universal hedge itself.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Rewrite every failure-completeness quantifier over compatible two-law inputs, specify whether \(\eta\) is witness-specific or uniform, and make the induced-law equalities part of the predicate tested by the three-node audit.
Make the three-node gate a concrete finite deliverable: publish one rational response-function table, its EXT-ID terminal trace, exact source-row null vector, and verified common \(\epsilon,\eta\).

After the gate succeeds, prove a transfer lemma from an IDSB/EXT-ID terminal obstruction to a graph-compatible response-fiber construction; this would turn the projective certificate from a fixed-representation fact into the genuinely field-level necessity route.
